input.quote: 5. PERSONNEL. Each party agrees to assign one (1) existing sales or marketing employee primarily dedicated to assist in the sales and marketing promotional activity set forth in this Exhibit D.
input.rationale: Compliant at the preferred position: no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant binds Corio (our party, the licensee/customer). Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit", "induce", "employ" and "employees" return no restrictive covenant, and each personnel-related provision is benign — Exhibit D §5 (p0203) is a staffing-assignment commitment; §§13.1-13.3 require Commerce One to give Corio access to its operations, consulting and engineering personnel; §13.5 (p0116) covers only confidentiality and invention-assignment agreements for Commerce One staff; §14.5 (p0126) is standard independent-contractor status language; and §14.10 (p0133) integrates only the concurrently executed NDA and the Statement of Work, so no non-solicit is imported by reference. Because there is no non-solicit clause to measure, the deterministic duration and general-solicitation carve-out checks are inapplicable rather than defective, and no redline or counterparty comment is proposed. Noted internally, not as a negotiation issue: if Commerce One later proposes a personnel covenant we would hold to the fallback (mutual, 12 months from the end of involvement, services personnel only, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire); the separately executed NDA was not available for review, so it should be checked for a buried non-solicit.
